summary: Close an iterator by conditionally invoking its return method and validating the returned object.

target.notes: Looks up return at close time; if absent, propagates the completion. If present, calls with iterator as this and requires an object result.

caveats: C# foreach disposal is not equivalent to JavaScript IteratorClose and does not reproduce dynamic return lookup or result validation.

tests.name: break calls return
tests.input: let closed=false; const it={next(){return {value:1,done:false}},return(){closed=true;return {done:true}},[Symbol.iterator](){return this}}; for(const x of it){break} console.log(closed);

tests.name: primitive return result on break throws
tests.input: const it={next(){return {value:1,done:false}},return(){return 1},[Symbol.iterator](){return this}}; try{for(const x of it){break}}catch(e){console.log(e.name)}
